This appeal is listed for non-filing of paper book.
The consent of the parties the paper book is dispensed with.
The appeal is taken up for consideration.

2. This appeal is admitted on 26.03.2024 to answer the following substantial questions of law:
(i) Whether the first appellate Court is justified in modifying the share allotted by the trial Court?
(ii) Whether the judgment and decree passed by the first appellate Court is opposed to the NC: 2024:KHC-K:5900 principles laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Vineeta Sharma Vs. Rakesh Sharma and others reported in (2020) 9 SCC 1?

sentences.text: (iii) What order or decree?
3. The admitted factual possession is that one Shivalingappa was the propositus.
He died in he year 1959.
Through his first wife, he had one daughter by name Nagawwaa who is the plaintiff.
After demise of his first wife, he married Basawwa.
Basawwa had a son by name Babu.
Basawwa died in the year 2008.
The suit is filed by the plaintiff, who is the daughter of propositus Shivalingappa from his first wife.
The plaintiff claims half share in the suit schedule properties.
4. The Trial Court granted half share in the suit schedule properties.
5. The defendant filed an appeal before the first Appellate Court and the appeal is allowed in part.
The First Appellate Court awarded 1/9th share to the plaintiff by making notional partition under Section 6 of Hindu Succession Act, during the life time of the father of Shivalingappa.

The NC:
2024:KHC-K:5900 daughter is awarded share in the share of father of Shivalingappa.
Aggrieved by the said judgment and decree the plaintiff is in the second regular appeal.

sentences.text: Since, the relationship of the parties is not in dispute and the second marriage of Shivalingappa has taken place after the death of the first wife, the daughter from first wife Nagawwa is also class-I heir and she is entitled to equal share on the demise of Shivalingappa.
On the death of Shivalingappa, Nagawwa had 1/3rd share along with Basawwa, the second wife and Babu son of Shivalingappa from his second wife.
Thus, the plaintiff would be entitled to 1/3rd share.

However,
the Trial Court has granted half share to the plaintiff as the heir of Basawwa along with the first defendant.
Since, the plaintiff is the daughter from first wife she does not become heir to the estate of late Basawwa.
7. The First Appellate Court erred in effecting notional partition.

Section 6 of Hindu Succession Act,
1956 is amended and the amendment has retrospectives effect.
Thus, Nagawwa is entitled to an equal share after the demise of Shivalingappa, and Nagawwa is entitled to 1/3rd share in the suit properties.
For the aforementioned reasons the impugned judgment and decree passed by the First Appellate Court as well as the Trial Court are set aside.
Hence, the following.
I. The appeal is allowed.
II. The suit of the plaintiff is decreed in part.
III. The judgment and decree dated 27.03.2017 In RA No.117/2016 on the file of III Additional District Judge, Vijayapur are set aside.
IV. The judgment and decree dated 28.07.2016 in OS No.342/2011 on the file of Senior Civil Judge Basavana Bagevadi are set aside.
V. The suit of the plaintiff is decreed in part, awarding 1/3rd share in the suit schedule properties.
VI. No order as to costs.
VII. It is stated that all the suit schedule properties are required and compensation is awarded.
The NC: 2024:KHC-K:5900 plaintiff is entitled to 1/3rd share in the compensation with all consequential benefits.
